sport.title: ATP Chiefs Under Fire For Skipping Doubles Trophy Presentation At Year-End Finals
paras: Henry Patten has criticised leading figures at the ATP for their absence from the year-end No. 1 doubles trophy presentation, which was presented to him and partner Harri Heliovaara. The British-Finnish duo was recognised for their achievements this season, including winning Wimbledon and reaching the French Open final.

They have also won four other titles since January. On Monday afternoon, the duo was presented with their trophy at the ATP Finals in Turin. However, both ATP chairman Andrea Guadenzi and CEO ​Eno Polo were not in attendance. “For us, it’s a really big deal.

sport.title: The five players who earned the most prize money on the WTA Tour in 2026 following Mirra Andreeva’s WTA Finals
paras: Mirra Andreeva received a healthy sum after capturing her first WTA Finals title on Sunday. The Russian youngster, who went undefeated at the event, earned $3,370,000 for her efforts in Indian Wells, California.

Andreeva’s triumph in the US capped what has been a truly memorable year on the WTA Tour – one defined by the successes of Andreeva and three-time major champion Elena Rybakina. With the season coming to an end, let us take a look at the WTA’s final prize money standings for the year. It has been a career-defining year for Kazakhstani star Elena Rybakina.

sport.title: Elina Svitolina now praises Mirra Andreeva and says what is ‘incredible’ about her after their WTA Finals matc
paras: Mirra Andreeva played some of the best tennis of her career to win the WTA Finals title last week. The Russian youngster, only 19 years old, did not drop a set en route to winning the end-of-year event, beating Elina Svitolina [twice], Aryna Sabalenka, Diana Shnaider and Jessica Pegula.

Andreeva capped her impressive week with victory against Svitolina in Sunday’s final . The teenager triumphed 7-5, 6-3 in Indian Wells, California. Svitolina, who also enjoyed an impressive campaign amid troubles in her personal life , heavily praised her triumphant opponent in the aftermath of Sunday’s showdown.

sport.title: November 17, 1991: The day Pete Sampras claimed his first season-ending ATP Masters Cup
paras: On this day in tennis history, one young American beat a compatriot to win his first ATP Masters Cup. Look back on how he did it

On this day, November 17, 1991, in Frankfurt, Pete Sampras beat Jim Courier in the final (3-6, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4) to claim his first title at the season-ending Masters Cup . For the young American, who had lost his US Open crown two months earlier – to the same opponent – it was a relief to win such an important title after a hard season.
